title: One Writer, Many Workers
hook: Why PING has exactly one writer to its canonical event journal.
thesis: The episode walks the chain Intent, then Policy, then Capability, then Durable Intent, then Execution, then Verification, then Evidence, and contrasts it with the failure: Worker goes straight to database INSERT. One sovereign mechanism per consequential decision: one canonical event writer, one identity rule per identity domain, one canonicalization contract, one capability decision path, one evidence verification contract. And the opposite lesson: a god-object EventAuthority that owned construction, persistence, sequencing, transport, query, and replay would violate the same principle.

proven: The directive states the one-writer position and the intent-to-evidence chain (sections 4, 5).
The directive states the god-object rejection: construction, persistence, sequencing, transport, query, replay are separate responsibilities (section 5).
partial: That the single canonical writer is the live enforcement boundary in the current codebase.
unknown: The exact writer implementation and any competing writer paths that would weaken the claim.

approval_gate: Nolan approves every exact post. Silence is not approval.
